newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares rise, seen in flat trend.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares rise, seen in flat trend.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse extended Thursday's moderate gains but analysts saw little potential for further growth and expected a flat session on Monday.

"I could bet that any change in the index (on Monday) will not be more than one percent in either direction, though maybe it will be slightly up," said Kamil Kalemba, a trader at ING Baring Securities in Warsaw.

Analysts said the bourse was likely to swing in a horizontal trend in the longer term as large privatisations and the forthcoming general elections were hampering buying while investors were reluctant to sell, expecting growth afterwards.
The main market's WIG index rose 0.6 percent to 16,382.3 and turnover rose 9.6 percent to 194.7 million zlotys on all three markets as 47 issues rose, 35 fell and 15 were flat.
Analysts said the Polish economy still had good growth prospects, which should prevent any significant falls on the exchange, and put psychological support at 16,000 points, resistance at 17,000.

Some banks rose for the third session running on Friday after their weak performance in the last three months, but analysts said their upside was limited as they were showing unspectacular financial results in 1997.
Analysts said the late May privatisation of Poland's largest commercial bank, Bank Handlowy SA, was additionally discouraging investors from buying listed banks.
They said the sale of Polish copper giant KGHM, planned for June, could also draw some capital from the bourse.
Espebepe trade was suspended on Friday as the firm's creditors are meeting to decide on a possible debt-write-off deal. -- Malgorzata Rzepka +48 22 653 9700
